findings.summary: Section 5 "Untracked Files Survive" is printed before section 4 "Where Work Dies", so the reader meets "survive" with no stated threat and the numbering runs 3 → 5 → 4.
findings.evidence: Page 2 ends with `{"type":"heading","text":"5. Untracked Files Survive"}` + `git clean -nd  # preview what would die`; page 3 then opens `{"type":"heading","text":"4. Where Work Dies","ink":"red"}` with "`--hard` is the only mode that destroys uncommitted work".
findings.fix: Move the "5. Untracked Files Survive" heading and its `git clean` code block to page 3, placing it after "4. Where Work Dies", and retitle it "5. Untracked Files Survive `--hard`" so the subject is explicit.

findings.summary: Page 3 ends with a headingless code block using `git commit --amend --no-edit` and `--force-with-lease`, both of which are only defined on page 4.
findings.evidence: Last block of page 3: `["git commit --amend --no-edit","git push --force-with-lease  # not --force"]`; page 4 later introduces "2. Amend Is A Mini-Rewrite" and "`--force-with-lease` refuses if the remote moved since your fetch".
findings.fix: Delete that code block from page 3 and place it on page 4 directly under "2. Amend Is A Mini-Rewrite", above the `--force-with-lease` bullets that explain it.

findings.summary: Page 4 closes with two reflog bullets (`main@{1}`, `git reflog show <branch>`) a full page before the reflog is introduced or `@{n}` notation is explained.
findings.evidence: Final blocks of page 4: "`main@{1}` reads a branch's own log, not HEAD's" and "`git reflog show <branch>` scopes output to one ref"; page 5 then starts the chapter with "1. What It Records — Every movement of HEAD and of each branch ref" and only there defines `HEAD@{n}` / `main@{1}` in the "3. Addressing Positions" table.
findings.fix: Move both bullets to page 5, appending them to the "3. Addressing Positions" section where `main@{1}` is first defined.

findings.summary: The recovery chapter runs 1 → 2 → 4 → (page break) → step-1 bullets → 3 → step-4 bullets, so both section 1 and section 4 are split around an intervening section.
findings.evidence: Page 5 heading order is "1. Three-Step Rescue", "2. Take Just One Commit", "4. When Reflog Cannot Help"; page 6 then opens with the step-1 bullets "Look for the op just before the loss: reset, rebase, branch -D" / "`git log <sha> -3` shows context before you commit to it", followed by "3. findings.fix: Reorder to 1 (code + its three bullets together on page 5), 2, 3 Deleted Branch, then 4 with the `git fsck --full --no-reflogs --unreachable --lost-found` block immediately followed by its four explanatory bullets on page 6.

findings.summary: The section heading "3. Undo Merge Or Pull" sits at the bottom of page 7 with no content beneath it; its table starts at the top of page 8.
findings.evidence: Page 7 left column ends with the heading "→ 3. Undo Merge Or Pull" followed by roughly 200px of empty column before the "#dev #notes 7/7" footer, while page 8 opens with the orphaned table "situation | fix — Merge, unpushed | git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD".
findings.fix: Keep the heading with its first block when paginating (treat a heading as non-breakable with the following element), pushing "3. Undo Merge Or Pull" to page 8 above its table.

findings.summary: "A fresh clone therefore has an empty reflog" is false: clone writes an initial reflog entry for HEAD and the checked-out branch.
findings.evidence: "Strictly local: never pushed, never cloned", "A fresh clone therefore has an empty reflog"
findings.fix: Change to: "A fresh clone starts with a single `clone: from <url>` entry — none of the origin repo's history of ref moves comes with it."

findings.summary: The `git restore` chapter's "Deleted A File?" callout opens the reflog page, one page after the restore section it belongs to has ended.
findings.evidence: Page 5 has `"page_title":"The Reflog: Every Move HEAD Made"` yet its first block is the callout "Deleted A File?" — "`git restore <path>` brings a tracked file back… But `git restore .` discards every unstaged edit".
findings.fix: Move this callout to page 4, immediately after "5. restore Cheat Rows"/"6. Legacy And switch".

findings.summary: Claim that `git fsck --lost-found` turns dangling commits into refs is wrong — they are written as plain files under `.git/lost-found/commit/`, not refs.
findings.evidence: "Commits become refs; dangling blobs become SHA-named files" (with "Findings land in `.git/lost-found/`")
findings.fix: Reword to: "Commits land as SHA-named files in `.git/lost-found/commit/`; blobs land in `.git/lost-found/other/` with their contents inside" — and note you still need `git branch <name> <sha>` to make a commit reachable.

findings.summary: The move-commit-to-another-branch recipe drops newly added files because `git stash pop` without `--index` leaves them untracked, and `git commit -a` does not stage untracked files.
findings.evidence: "git reset --soft HEAD~1  # wrong branch", "git stash", "git switch right-branch", "git stash pop && git commit -a"
findings.fix: Use `git stash pop --index` (restores the staged state, including added files) and then `git commit`, or replace `git commit -a` with `git add -A && git commit`.

findings.summary: A stash/branch mistakes table and the wrong-branch fix code block sit unheaded under page 7's "3. Undo Merge Or Pull" heading, mixing the Common Mistakes chapter into the merge/pull section.
findings.evidence: Page 8 blocks 2 and 3, between the merge/pull table and "4. Secrets And Debris", are a `Mistake | Fix` table ("Pop hit conflicts", "`stash clear` regret", "Branch deleted with -D") and `git reset --soft HEAD~1  # wrong branch` — neither has a heading, and page 7's last heading is "3. Undo Merge Or Pull".
findings.fix: Move both blocks to sit with "6. Mistake, Then Fix" at the end of page 8 (or give them their own numbered heading), leaving only the merge/pull table under "3. Undo Merge Or Pull".

findings.summary: The pull-undo row uses the `@{u}` upstream shorthand, which is never defined anywhere in the handbook.
findings.evidence: Page 8 table row: `["Pull, match upstream","`git reset --hard @{u}`"]` — no prior or later block explains `@{u}`.
findings.fix: Expand the row to `git reset --hard @{u}` with a gloss such as "`@{u}` = the branch's upstream, e.g. `origin/main`", or add that as a bullet under the same section.

findings.summary: The safety-ranking flow diagram gives no direction label, so a learner cannot tell which end is safest.
findings.evidence: `{"type":"heading","text":"4. Safety Ranking"}` followed by `{"type":"diagram","kind":"flow","spec":{"nodes":["revert","restore --staged",…,"clean -fdx"]}}` with no "safest → most destructive" wording anywhere on the page.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading "4. Safety Ranking: Safest → Most Destructive" (or label the diagram's two ends) so the direction of the flow is stated.
